title: Wine Wimsey Review · Fri Nov 27
subtitle: NEW-VOICE batch 5. Replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 27 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder. 8 character feed posts (4 then-vs-now two-panel story cards in slots 1,3,5,7 modeled on the doctor/Barb winner; 4 rip-off posts alternating close-up and scene) + 2 stories. Zero plain cards. #08 remade Nov 26 afternoon after Scott rejected the casserole pet-peeve card; new #08 is a rip-off scene card (optical upsell / Stephanie). Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and 2 stories and said upload on Nov 26. First-comment delays randomized (0-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: In 1986 a teller named Linda knew my name and had a lollipop for my kids. / Now the bank app locked me out for a 'new device.' / Same phone. I've had it since March.
posts.caption: Linda also remembered my mother's maiden name without asking me for it. Yesterday I answered three security questions, got a six-digit code, and the code expired while I was typing it.
posts.first: I ended up driving to the branch. There's a kiosk where Linda's window used to be.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her smiling at the teller window as Linda hands a lollipop over the counter; now: twitchy gritted-teeth grimace, holding the phone up like evidence). posts.quote: My niece Kayla got a $50 gift card for her birthday. / She left it in a drawer for a year. / Now it's worth $38.50 because of an 'inactivity fee.' / Apparently the card pays rent now.
posts.caption: The fine print was on the back in letters the size of a sesame seed. I read it with my glasses, a flashlight and my sister on speaker, and it still made no sense.
posts.first: Kayla spent the whole $38.50 on lunch that afternoon. I taught her well.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (one raised eyebrow smirk, dangling the gift card between two fingers like garbage). posts.quote: In 1983 Gus at the hardware store walked you right to the screw you needed. / Now the app sends me to aisle 37, bay 12. / The hook is empty.
posts.caption: Gus could hold up your broken hinge, squint at it, and say 'three-eighths' without looking at a box. The only employee I found was a teenager in a vest who was looking for aisle 37 too.
posts.first: I ordered the screws online and they come Tuesday. The cabinet door is leaning against the wall until then.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her nodding as Gus holds up the right screw; now: slow eye-roll, phone held out at an empty shelf hook). Text at the top reads: In 1983 gus at the hardware store walked you right to the screw you needed. now the app sends me to aisle 37, bay 12. A red box at the bottom reads: The hook is empty.

posts.quote: The movie said 7:00. / We sat through 24 minutes of ads and trailers. / Barb finished her $11 popcorn before the opening credits.
posts.caption: Two tickets were $32 and the water was $6. The man behind us kicked my seat through every single trailer, which I suppose was the free part.
posts.first: The movie was good, for the record. Next time I'm bringing a book for the first half hour.

posts.quote: In 1984 picture day was $8 and a comb in my son's back pocket. / Now my grandson's 'basic package' is $42, / and retouching is another $12.
posts.caption: My son's 1984 picture had a cowlick, a missing tooth and a laser background, and it's still on my fridge. Tyler's proof came with a $9.99 'background upgrade.'
posts.first: I ordered the smallest package and one wallet size for me. Tyler's cowlick was free.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her combing her little son's hair before picture day; now: open-mouth 'are you kidding me' squint, holding the order form up like evidence). posts.quote: I returned a lamp I never opened, still taped shut. / The store charged me a $7.95 'restocking fee.' / Kyle put it right back on the shelf. I watched him.
posts.caption: The receipt was in the bag, the tape was never cut, and the price sticker was still on the box. Restocking, as far as I could tell, took Kyle about four steps.
posts.first: I'm not mad at Kyle. Kyle doesn't make the rules, he just walks them back to aisle 6.

posts.quote: In 1982 downtown parking was a quarter and a meter maid named Dot who'd let it slide. / Now it's $2.75, an app, and a five-digit zone number / to return one library book.
posts.caption: Dot drove a little three-wheel cart and knew every car on Main Street. The app wanted my email, my license plate and a password with a symbol in it, and the book was already late.
posts.first: I paid the 40-cent late fee at the desk in person. It was the cheapest part of the whole trip.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses (young-her dropping a quarter in the meter while Dot waves; now: tight fake 'everything is fine' smile, tapping her phone at the parking sign). posts.quote: The frames were $149 and the lenses were $129. / Then Stephanie added $89 for anti-glare. / I came in for a pair of readers.
posts.caption: The scratch-resistant coating was another $49, and the hard case was $12. My old readers were $8 at the drugstore and they still work, they just aren't pretty.
posts.first: I bought the frames and the basic lenses and walked out. My $8 drugstore pair is still in my purse.
